born.why: The code analyzes historical data for each item kind 'k' to determine if interacting with it lowers or raises n1 (health/danger level); it actively pursues items that have previously reduced n1 and avoids those that increased it, defaulting to conservative actions when history is absent or n1 is critically high.

The previous code blindly followed the default choice `x.n5`, which led to repeated high-impact interactions (k=422, amount 1) that kept n1 elevated but didn't kill the agent, yet failed to optimize for longevity by not actively managing risk when n1 spiked. The new code introduces a safety buffer: if n1 is critically high (>90), it forces a low-impact option ('a3') to prevent death; if n1 is very low (<10), it becomes more aggressive/trusting of the default to build reserves; otherwise, it monitors recent "near-death" events (n1 > 95) in history `z` and switches to conservative mode if any occurred, ensuring survival during dangerous phases while exploiting safe periods.

The code identifies k=110 as consistently dangerous (increasing n1) and forces avoidance by swapping the default action, while permitting interaction with other item kinds that either reduce n1 or are neutral, prioritizing survival by eliminating the known fatal pattern.

The previous code blindly followed the default choice, leading to death via high n1 accumulation from repeated risky items (k=634). This version avoids taking dangerous defaults when n1 is high and uses item history to validate safety before approaching or accepting choices, prioritizing survival by filtering out items that cause large n1 spikes.
